rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is entirely absent, so the first experiment should test a representative multimodal configuration with standard encoders (pca_n2000 for RNA and imagenet_vit_l for images) and simple fusion (concat). This clarifies whether multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines and provides initial insights into encoder and fusion method effectiveness.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, singleprofile) achieves 0.535 accuracy. Uncertainty remains about whether singleprofile vs multiprofile settings, or different fusion/aggregation methods, yield better results. Testing config_015 (multimodal, singleprofile) with scgpt RNA and resnet50 image encoders (vs pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l in config_001) clarifies if encoder choices impact performance. This balances exploration of encoder alternatives with maintaining the singleprofile setting, which may be more promising than multiprofile given limited budget.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal singleprofile models with ViT image encoder (config_001) achieve 0.535 accuracy. This experiment tests using scgpt RNA encoder (a more advanced model) with the same ViT image encoder and weighted fusion, which may improve performance. It clarifies whether upgrading the RNA encoder and fusion method can surpass the current best, balancing exploitation of the ViT image encoder with exploration of better RNA encoders.

Existing evidence shows that pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoders with concat fusion (config_001) achieve the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests the same encoders but with multiprofile setting and transformer aggregation, exploring if this combination can yield better results while balancing exploration of multiprofile and exploitation of proven components.

The existing evidence shows config_034 (0.5988 accuracy) is the best so far with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, vit_l image, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 RNA with scgpt (a more sophisticated encoder) and switching fusion from concat to weighted, which could improve performance. It balances exploration (testing new RNA encoder and fusion) while building on the successful transformer aggregation from config_034. This clarifies whether scgpt and weighted fusion can further enhance accuracy, leveraging the strong foundation of transformer aggregation.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation (e.g., config_034) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.5988). This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the same multiprofile setup (using pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l) could further improve performance. It clarifies the impact of fusion methods on accuracy while retaining the proven aggregation strategy, balancing exploration and exploitation.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile settings with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_046) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests using resnet50 as the image encoder with these components, which could improve performance by leveraging a different image encoder while maintaining the promising aggregation and fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using 'transformer' aggregation and 'imagenet_vit_l' image encoder (e.g., config_034) achieve high accuracy (0.5988). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from 'pca_n2000' to 'scvi_n200' while keeping the same image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice impacts performance, as 'scvi_n200' may offer better representation. It is the best use of the remaining budget to explore a promising direction with minimal changes to a top-performing setup.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_047) achieve high accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests changing fusion from concat to weighted while keeping other parameters the same, clarifying if fusion method impacts performance. It's the best use of the last budget as it directly explores a critical design choice in the top-performing architecture.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_043) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests a similar setup with aggregation None, clarifying if the aggregation method is critical. It is the best use of the last budget slot to explore a closely related configuration with potential for higher accuracy.
